abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective combination chemotherapy has improved the previously dismal prognosis for malignant ovarian germ cell tumors (MOGCT) dramatically. In young patients, conservative surgery with adjuvant chemotherapy has made the preservation of fertility possible, even in patients with advanced disease. The increase in cure rates has shifted the focus of recent studies to the long term menstrual, reproductive, and gynecologic outcomes in these patients. METHODS: The current study is a retrospective review of 74 patients with MOGCT treated by conservative surgery, retaining the uterus and contralateral ovary to preserve ovarian function, with or without chemotherapy. RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 20.9 years (range, 10-35 years). The histologic subtypes included 31 dysgerminomas (41.9%), 16 immature teratomas (21.6%), 13 endodermal sinus tumors (17.6%), 11 mixed germ cell tumors (14.9%), and 3 embryonal cell tumors (4.1%). There were 56 International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) Stage I tumors (75.7%), 3 Stage II tumors, (4.1%), 11 Stage III tumors (14.9%), and 4 Stage IV tumors (5.4%). Adjuvant chemotherapy was administered in 47 patients (63.5%). The overall mean follow-up period was 52.1 months. There were 7 recurrences (9.5%) and 2 deaths (2.7%). Survival for patients with Stage I disease was 98.2% and that for patients with advanced disease stages was 94.4%. During chemotherapy 61.7% of patients developed amenorrhea but 91.5% of these women resumed normal menstrual function on completion of chemotherapy. Fourteen healthy live births were recorded in the chemotherapy group and there were no documented birth defects. There was 1 case of infertility (1.4%). CONCLUSIONS: The surgical approach in young patients with MOGCT confined to a single ovary should aim to preserve fertility. Advanced disease is not usually accompanied by contralateral ovarian disease and should not necessarily contraindicate conservative surgery. The majority of these patients who have received combination chemotherapy resume normal ovarian function and can expect a normal fertility rate and healthy offspring.
abstract_ja: 背景：有効な併用化学療法により、従来は予後不良であった悪性卵巣胚細胞腫瘍(MOGCT)の治療成績は劇的に改善した。若年患者では、保存手術と補助化学療法により、進行例においても妊孕性の温存が可能となった。治癒率の向上に伴い、近年の研究の焦点は、これらの患者における長期的な月経、生殖、婦人科的転帰へと移っている。方法：子宮と対側卵巣を温存する保存手術を、化学療法の有無にかかわらず施行した悪性卵巣胚細胞腫瘍74例の後方視的レビューである。結果：平均年齢は20.9歳(範囲10～35歳)であった。組織型は、ディスジャーミノーマ（未分化胚細胞腫）31例(41.9%)、未熟奇形腫16例(21.6%)、卵黄嚢腫瘍13例(17.6%)、混合型胚細胞腫瘍11例(14.9%)、胎児性癌3例(4.1%)であった。国際産婦人科連合(FIGO)の病期は、病期I 56例(75.7%)、病期II 3例(4.1%)、病期III 11例(14.9%)、病期IV 4例(5.4%)であった。補助化学療法は47例(63.5%)に施行された。平均追跡期間は52.1か月であった。再発は7例(9.5%)、死亡は2例(2.7%)であった。病期I症例の生存率は98.2%、進行病期の症例では94.4%であった。化学療法中、61.7%の患者で無月経を生じたが、化学療法終了後にはこれらの女性の91.5%が正常な月経機能を回復した。化学療法群では健康な生児が14例得られ、先天異常の記録はなかった。不妊症は1例(1.4%)であった。結論：単一卵巣に限局した悪性卵巣胚細胞腫瘍の若年患者では、妊孕性を温存する手術を目指すべきである。進行例においても対側卵巣の病変を伴うことは通常なく、保存手術の禁忌とすべきではない。併用化学療法を受けた大多数の患者は正常な卵巣機能を回復し、正常な妊孕性と健康な子を期待できる。
